newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine coal imports seen doubling to 11 mln T.
newsitem.headline: Philippine coal imports seen doubling to 11 mln T.

text.p: Philippine coal imports are expected to more than double to 11.5 million tonnes by 2001 from the projected 5.1 million this year due to increasing demand from power and cement plants, an industry executive said on Thursday.
Coal demand in the country this year is expected to reach 6.26 million tonnes against domestic output of 1.15 million, said Francisco Aragon, president of the Philippie Chamber of Coal Mines.
By the year 2001, domestic coal output is seen reaching 1.75 million tonnes, he added.

"The Philippines will remain a net importer of coal on account of the inability of local coal producers to meet substantial growth rate in demand," Aragon said at a Philippine mining conference attended by government and industry officials.
The Philippines imported 2.983 million tonnes of coal last year, of which 1.965 million tonnes came from Indonesia. The rest came from Australia, China, Russia, South Africa and Vietnam.

Aragon said he expected coal demand by power firms to increase from 3.2 million tonnes this year to 8.65 million by the year 2001 while demand from cement firms is seen rising from 2.72 million tonnes to 4.24 million.
The government hopes to build more coal-fired power plants to increase capacity to 3,775 megawatts (MW) by 2001 from the existing 1,475.
Coal demand in the cement sector is also expected to increase due to entry of seven new plants and expansion programmes of the existing 19 plants.
The Department of Energy plans to implement an intensive coal exploration programme in eight regions in the country in the next five years.
"If these plans are implemented as scheduled, total proven coal reserves are expected to increase from the current 388 million tonnes to 630 million tonnes by the year 2001."
